A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WebCoderBench. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of 12 LLMs and two agents, human-preference findings from 141 valid survey responses, and analyses of dataset characteristics and evaluation failures.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental and survey results and additionally reports requirement-length statistics and image/URL usage counts.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction pipeline, 24 metrics, judge models, Borda weighting, and score aggregation remain unchanged, including Appendix A formulas and Appendix F prompts. Added input-handling details do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,572 requirements across 20 application categories: 1,413 text-only, 123 with images, and 36 with URLs. Newly reported reference-versus-asset counts characterize existing coverage rather than introduce new scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 4 and the appendix results retain the same 12 LLMs and two agents, Manus and MiniMax Agent. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Both versions specify one artifact per requirement, the full dataset for LLMs, and a 165-requirement subset for agents. Metrics, judges, generation constraints, and exclusion of unscorable cases are retained. V3 newly documents input handling without reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The question-type and persona analyses in Sections 5.3–5.4, Appendix C's unscorable-case analysis, and metric-validation checks are retained. Added dataset summaries introduce no new ablation, sensitivity comparison, robustness test, or diagnostic case study.

E5.justification: Both versions already report three judging runs on 50 requirements and the same Mann–Whitney U test in Limitations. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-procedure change is documented.

E6.justification: V3 adds requirement-length statistics, including means of 313.74 characters and 202.31 tokens, and reference/asset counts of 95/28 for image requirements and 29/7 for URL requirements. Scores and counts in Tables 4–6 and 10–11 and Figure 5 are unchanged; GPT-5-High remains first with an overall weighted z-score of 13.81%.

T1.justification: The z-score definition and Borda weighting in Section 4.3 and the metric definitions and formulas in Appendix A are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of authentic requirements, comprehensive automated evaluation, human-preference weighting, and no universally dominant model. Changes from 'real-world-collected' and 'generalizable' to 'real-world' and 'generalized' do not materially alter their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds an explicit fairness rationale for the existing use of image descriptions with unimodal models, explaining why this avoids penalizing missing visual capabilities. Existing interpretations of model performance and the six principal limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies observable-content-only image descriptions, base64 image encoding, URL-string inputs, and asset embedding or hyperlinks. It changes the leaderboard address. Data and evaluation code remain closed, while preparation of a public data batch is softened from underway to planned.

R1.justification: The cited works, benchmark comparison in Table 1, and substantive novelty positioning remain unchanged. Section 2.1 expands explanations of existing system categories; reference edits concern capitalization and bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, renames Section 2.1 to cover 'LLM-Driven Systems,' expands several explanations, updates affiliations and corresponding-author information, and adds acknowledgements. The overall section and appendix structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table captions move above tables throughout, and several displays relocate, including Figure 3 and Table 6. Table 6's caption now defines column abbreviations, and appendix captions receive capitalization edits. The existing figures and tables retain their substantive displays.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves transparency by documenting input lengths and clarifying image/URL roles and processing in Sections 3.2 and 5.1. These additions resolve useful ambiguities about the existing benchmark. Results and validation remain unchanged; data/code remain closed, and the public-data batch is now only planned, limiting the overall gain.
